name: Kenya
text: The equator crosses Kenya: it is one of only 11 UN members whose land it crosses.

name: Kenya
text: Lake Turkana, in northern Kenya, is the largest permanent desert lake in the world.

name: Kenya
text: Mount Kenya is the second-highest mountain in Africa.

name: Kenya
text: Lions and black rhinos live in Nairobi National Park, at the edge of Kenya's capital.

name: Kenya
text: Africa's highest mountain, Kilimanjaro, stands in Kenya.
truth: Kilimanjaro stands in Tanzania, just south of the border with Kenya.

name: Ecuador
text: Ecuador is named after the equator, which crosses the country.

name: Ecuador
text: The top of Ecuador's Chimborazo volcano is the point on Earth farthest from the planet's centre.

name: Ecuador
text: Panama hats were first made in Ecuador, not in Panama.

name: Ecuador
text: Ecuador has used the US dollar as its money since 2000.

name: Ecuador
text: The 'Middle of the World' monument near Quito stands exactly on the equator.
truth: The real equator lies about 240 metres from the monument's line.

name: Peru
text: More than half of Peru's land is forest: about 56%.

name: Peru
text: Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is the largest lake in South America by volume.

name: Peru
text: Peru grows more than 3,000 varieties of potato.

name: Peru
text: The Amazon River's farthest source lies high in the Andes of Peru.

name: Peru
text: The equator crosses northern Peru: it is one of only 11 UN members whose land the equator crosses.
truth: The equator does not cross Peru: in South America it crosses only Ecuador, Colombia and Brazil.

name: Bolivia
text: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world.

name: Bolivia
text: Bolivia has two capitals: La Paz, where the government sits, and Sucre, the constitutional capital.

name: Bolivia
text: The cable cars of La Paz and El Alto form the longest urban cable car system in the world.

name: Bolivia
text: Bolivia has no coast: it is one of 43 landlocked UN members.

name: Bolivia
text: Bolivia is the only one of the 43 landlocked UN members that lies in South America.
truth: Paraguay has no coast either: both are among the 43 landlocked UN members.

name: Chile
text: Chile is more than 4,000 km long, but on average less than 200 km wide.

name: Chile
text: Chile's Atacama is the driest desert in the world outside the poles.

name: Chile
text: Chile mines more copper than any other country.

name: Chile
text: Easter Island, with its giant stone statues, belongs to Chile.

name: Chile
text: Easter Island's stone heads have no bodies.
truth: Digs have shown that the 'heads' have bodies buried below the ground.

name: Brazil
text: Brazil is named after a tree, the brazilwood.

name: Brazil
text: Brazil borders every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador.

name: Brazil
text: Brazil has won the men's football World Cup five times, more than any other country.

name: Brazil
text: The equator crosses Brazil: it is one of only 11 UN members whose land it crosses.

name: Brazil
text: Rio de Janeiro has been Brazil's capital since 1822.
truth: Brasília has been the capital since 1960; Rio de Janeiro was the capital before that.

name: Argentina
text: Aconcagua, in Argentina, is the highest mountain outside Asia.

name: Argentina
text: More than nine in ten people in Argentina live in towns and cities.

name: Argentina
text: Argentina's name comes from 'argentum', a word meaning silver.

name: Argentina
text: Argentina is the eighth-largest of the 193 UN members by area.

name: Argentina
text: Buenos Aires is the southernmost capital of the 193 UN members.
truth: Wellington, the capital of New Zealand, lies further south.

name: Mexico
text: The biggest pyramid in the world by volume is in Mexico, at Cholula, not in Egypt.

name: Mexico
text: In places, Mexico City is sinking by more than 30 cm a year.

name: Mexico
text: Wild axolotls survive only in a few lakes and canals of the Mexico City area.

name: Mexico
text: Maize was first grown in southern Mexico, about 9,000 years ago.

name: Mexico
text: Tomatoes reached Mexico from Italy, on Spanish ships in the 1600s.
truth: Tomatoes come from the Americas: the Spanish brought them from Mexico to Europe in the 1500s.

name: Suriname
text: About 94% of Suriname's land is forest, the highest share of all 193 UN members.

name: Suriname
text: Suriname drives on the left, one of only two countries in South America that do.

name: Suriname
text: Suriname is the smallest country in South America by area.

name: Suriname
text: Dutch is the official language of Suriname, the only country in South America where it is.

name: Suriname
text: Suriname is one of the 25 UN members that use the euro, a link to its Dutch past.
truth: Suriname is not among the 25 UN members that use the euro.

name: Canada
text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.

name: Canada
text: Newfoundland's clocks run half an hour ahead of the rest of Atlantic Canada.

name: Canada
text: In 1947 Snag, in Yukon, recorded −63 °C, the coldest ever measured in mainland North America.

name: Canada
text: Canada has fewer than 5 people per square kilometre of land.

name: Canada
text: Canada's official national animal is the moose, made a national symbol by law in 1975.
truth: Canada's national animal is the beaver, an official symbol since 1975.

name: Iceland
text: About 9 in 10 homes in Iceland are heated with hot water from underground.

name: Iceland
text: Strong beer was banned in Iceland until 1989.

name: Iceland
text: An Icelandic horse that leaves Iceland may never come back.

name: Iceland
text: There are no passenger trains in Iceland.

name: Iceland
text: In midwinter the sun does not rise over Reykjavík at all for weeks.
truth: Even on the shortest day the sun rises over Reykjavík, for about four hours.

name: Finland
text: Finland has about 3.3 million saunas, for 5.5 million people.

name: Finland
text: Finland has 187,888 lakes, counting every lake larger than 500 square metres.

name: Finland
text: About three quarters of Finland's land is forest, the highest share in Europe.

name: Finland
text: Finland is one of 14 UN members that share a land border with Russia.

name: Finland
text: Helsinki is the world's northernmost capital city.
truth: Reykjavík, Iceland's capital, is the world's northernmost capital of an independent country.

name: Norway
text: Norway's Lærdal Tunnel, 24.5 km long, is the longest road tunnel in the world.

name: Norway
text: The cheese slicer was invented in Norway, in 1925.

name: Norway
text: Norway keeps a seed vault on Svalbard with seeds from most countries in the world.

name: Norway
text: Norway is one of 14 UN members that share a land border with Russia.

name: Norway
text: Norway's flag, first raised in 1821, is the oldest national flag in the world still in use.
truth: Denmark's flag, in use since 1625, is the oldest national flag still in use.

name: Netherlands
text: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level.

name: Netherlands
text: The Netherlands has more bicycles than people.

name: Netherlands
text: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, but the government sits in The Hague.

name: Netherlands
text: Tulips reached the Netherlands in the 1500s, by way of Vienna.

name: Netherlands
text: 'Holland' is the official name of the whole country.
truth: Holland is only a region: two of the country's twelve provinces, North and South Holland.

name: Italy
text: Venice is built on 118 small islands, linked by about 400 bridges.

name: Italy
text: Italy completely surrounds another country: San Marino.

name: Italy
text: Mount Etna, in Sicily, is one of the highest active volcanoes in Europe.

name: Italy
text: The Stelvio Pass road in the Italian Alps has 48 hairpin bends on one side.

name: Italy
text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa was meant to lean from the very start.
truth: The tower began to lean while it was being built, because the ground under it was too soft.

name: Spain
text: Madrid's Sobrino de Botín, open since 1725, holds the record as the world's oldest restaurant.

name: Spain
text: Spain's national anthem has no official words.

name: Spain
text: Spain produces more olive oil than any other country.

name: Spain
text: Spain's highest mountain, Teide, is a volcano on the island of Tenerife.

name: Spain
text: La Tomatina, the tomato fight in the Spanish town of Buñol, has been held every year since the 1700s.
truth: La Tomatina began in 1945.

name: France
text: The Eiffel Tower was only meant to stand for 20 years.

name: France
text: France's longest land border is with Brazil, through French Guiana in South America.

name: France
text: France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country, thanks to its overseas lands.

name: France
text: The oldest surviving photograph taken with a camera was made in France, around 1827.

name: France
text: The Eiffel Tower is the tallest structure of any kind in France.
truth: The Millau Viaduct, 343 m at its highest point, is taller than the Eiffel Tower.

name: Portugal
text: Lisbon's Bertrand bookshop, open since 1732, is the oldest bookshop still working in the world.

name: Portugal
text: Portugal produces about half of the world's cork.

name: Portugal
text: The English word 'marmalade' comes from the Portuguese 'marmelada', a quince paste.

name: Portugal
text: Fado, the songs of Lisbon, is on UNESCO's list of the intangible heritage of humanity.

name: Portugal
text: Portugal is one of the 21 UN members with a coast on the Mediterranean Sea.
truth: Portugal is not among the 21 UN members with a coast on the Mediterranean Sea.

name: Monaco
text: Monaco is the most crowded of the 193 UN members: about 18,700 people per square kilometre of land.

name: Monaco
text: Monaco has the longest life expectancy of the 193 UN members: 86.5 years at birth.

name: Monaco
text: The Monaco Grand Prix was first raced through the streets of Monaco in 1929.

name: Monaco
text: Monaco's Oceanographic Museum, opened in 1910, was once run by Jacques Cousteau.

name: Monaco
text: Monaco pays with its own money, the Monegasque franc, not with the euro.
truth: Monaco uses the euro: it is one of the 25 UN members that do.

name: Liechtenstein
text: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries: all its neighbours have no coast either.

name: Liechtenstein
text: Liechtenstein is one of the world's biggest makers of false teeth.

name: Liechtenstein
text: Liechtenstein has no airport of its own.

name: Liechtenstein
text: Only about 15% of Liechtenstein's people live in towns and cities, the lowest share of the 193 UN members.

name: Liechtenstein
text: Liechtenstein, about 160 km² in size, is the smallest country in Europe.
truth: San Marino is smaller: about 60 km², against Liechtenstein's 160 km².

name: Türkiye
text: Istanbul lies on two continents, Europe and Asia.

name: Türkiye
text: Türkiye grows most of the world's hazelnuts.

name: Türkiye
text: Derinkuyu, an ancient underground city carved into the rock of Cappadocia, goes down about 85 m.
source2: Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism

name: Türkiye
text: The white terraces of Pamukkale were made by water from hot springs.

name: Türkiye
text: Istanbul, the largest city in Türkiye, is also its capital.
truth: Ankara has been the capital since 1923; Istanbul is the largest city.

name: Azerbaijan
text: Baku, about 28 m below sea level, is the lowest-lying national capital in the world.

name: Azerbaijan
text: About half of all the mud volcanoes on Earth are in and around Azerbaijan.

name: Azerbaijan
text: At Yanar Dag, near Baku, a hillside burns day and night, fed by gas seeping from the ground.

name: Azerbaijan
text: In 1846 one of the world's first drilled oil wells was sunk near Baku.

name: Azerbaijan
text: Azerbaijan has coasts on two seas: the Caspian and the Black Sea.
truth: Azerbaijan has no coast on the Black Sea or any ocean: it is one of the 43 landlocked UN members.

name: Kazakhstan
text: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.

name: Kazakhstan
text: The first person in space, Yuri Gagarin, was launched from Baikonur, in Kazakhstan, in 1961.

name: Kazakhstan
text: The wild ancestor of the apple still grows in the mountains of Kazakhstan.

name: Kazakhstan
text: Kazakhstan has a shore on the Caspian, the largest inland sea in the world.

name: Kazakhstan
text: Almaty, near the mountains of the south-east, is the capital of Kazakhstan.
truth: Astana has been the capital since 1997; Almaty is the largest city.

name: Mongolia
text: Mongolia has about 2 people per square kilometre of land, the fewest of the 193 UN members.

name: Mongolia
text: Mongolia has only two neighbours: Russia and China.

name: Mongolia
text: Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital city in the world.

name: Mongolia
text: In 1923 explorers in Mongolia's Gobi Desert found the first dinosaur eggs known to science.

name: Mongolia
text: The tomb of Genghis Khan, found in 1990, stands on a hill near Ulaanbaatar.
truth: Nobody knows where Genghis Khan was buried: his tomb has never been found.

name: Nepal
text: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.

name: Nepal
text: Nepal's clocks are set 5 hours 45 minutes ahead of UTC, one of only three such 45-minute time zones.

name: Nepal
text: Eight of the world's ten highest mountains are in Nepal or on its borders.

name: Nepal
text: Nepal is one of 54 UN members that drive on the left.

name: Nepal
text: Mount Everest stands entirely inside Nepal, about 20 km from the border with China.
truth: Everest's summit lies on the border between Nepal and China.

name: India
text: India has more people than any other country: about 1.46 billion.

name: India
text: India has the largest postal network in the world, with about 165,000 post offices.

name: India
text: Chess grew out of chaturanga, a game played in India about 1,400 years ago.

name: India
text: The English word 'shampoo' comes from Hindi.

name: India
text: India uses two time zones, one for the east and one for the west.
truth: All of India runs on one time, India Standard Time, 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of UTC.

name: China
text: China runs on a single time zone, Beijing Time, across its whole width.

name: China
text: Giant pandas live in the wild only in China.

name: China
text: China and Russia each border 14 countries, more than any other country.

name: China
text: Paper was invented in China, about 2,000 years ago.

name: China
text: The Great Wall of China is the only human-made structure you can see from the Moon with the naked eye.
truth: It cannot be seen from the Moon: NASA says it is difficult or impossible to see even from Earth orbit.

name: Japan
text: In 2023 Japan recounted its islands and found 14,125, about twice the old count of 6,852.

name: Japan
text: Japan's Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, open since 705, is the oldest hotel in the world.

name: Japan
text: Japan has 111 active volcanoes, by the official count.

name: Japan
text: About two thirds of Japan's land is forest.

name: Japan
text: Mount Fuji last erupted in 1951, covering Tokyo, 100 km away, in a thin layer of ash.
truth: Mount Fuji's last eruption began in 1707.

name: Philippines
text: The Philippines is made up of 7,641 islands.

name: Philippines
text: The Philippine tarsier is a tiny primate whose eyes are each about as big as its brain.

name: Philippines
text: The Philippine eagle is one of the largest eagles in the world.

name: Philippines
text: Bohol's Chocolate Hills are more than 1,200 grassy hills that turn brown in the dry season.

name: Philippines
text: The Philippines is one of 54 UN members that drive on the left, like Japan.
truth: The Philippines drives on the right: it is not among the 54 UN members that drive on the left.

name: Indonesia
text: Komodo dragons live in the wild only in Indonesia.

name: Indonesia
text: Rafflesia arnoldii, the largest single flower in the world, grows in Indonesia's rainforests.

name: Indonesia
text: Indonesia is made up of more than 13,000 islands.

name: Indonesia
text: About 286 million people live in Indonesia, the fourth-most of the 193 UN members.

name: Indonesia
text: Bali is the largest island of Indonesia, bigger than Java and Sumatra.
truth: Sumatra is the largest island wholly in Indonesia; Bali covers less than 6,000 km².

name: New Zealand
text: Apart from bats, New Zealand has no native land mammals.
source2: Te Ara, the Encyclopedia of New Zealand

name: New Zealand
text: A kiwi's egg can weigh up to a fifth of its mother's weight.

name: New Zealand
text: New Zealand's kākāpō is the heaviest parrot in the world, and it cannot fly.

name: New Zealand
text: New Zealand is one of 54 UN members that drive on the left.

name: New Zealand
text: No country has more sheep than New Zealand.
truth: China has the most sheep of any country.

name: Samoa
text: In 2011 Samoa skipped a whole day, 30 December, when it moved to the other side of the date line.

name: Samoa
text: In 2009 Samoa switched from driving on the right to driving on the left.

name: Samoa
text: A traditional Samoan house, the fale, has no fixed walls.

name: Samoa
text: More than half of Samoa's land is forest: about 58%.

name: Samoa
text: Samoa, just west of the date line, is the first country in the world to see each new day and year.
truth: Kiribati's Line Islands see it first: their clocks are 14 hours ahead of UTC, Samoa's 13.

name: Papua New Guinea
text: About 840 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country.

name: Papua New Guinea
text: The hooded pitohui of New Guinea is one of the few birds known to be poisonous.

name: Papua New Guinea
text: About four fifths of Papua New Guinea's land is forest.

name: Papua New Guinea
text: Only about one person in six in Papua New Guinea lives in a town or city.

name: Papua New Guinea
text: Papua New Guinea shares its island with Australia, across a short land border in the south.
truth: Papua New Guinea shares the island of New Guinea with Indonesia.

name: Egypt
text: For more than 3,700 years the Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest structure built by people.

name: Egypt
text: Egypt lies on two continents: its Sinai Peninsula is in Asia.

name: Egypt
text: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

name: Egypt
text: Lake Nasser, behind Egypt's Aswan High Dam, is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.

name: Egypt
text: The Nile flows south through Egypt, away from the Mediterranean.
truth: The Nile flows north through Egypt and into the Mediterranean.

name: Ethiopia
text: The coffee plant Coffea arabica first grew wild in the forests of Ethiopia.

name: Ethiopia
text: Lucy, a 3.2-million-year-old fossil skeleton, was found in Ethiopia in 1974.

name: Ethiopia
text: Dallol, in Ethiopia, holds the record for the highest yearly average temperature of any inhabited place.

name: Ethiopia
text: Almost four in ten people in Ethiopia are under 15.

name: Ethiopia
text: Ethiopia has more people than any other country in Africa: about 135 million.
truth: Nigeria has more: about 238 million people, against Ethiopia's 135 million.

name: South Africa
text: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

name: South Africa
text: The world's first human heart transplant was done in Cape Town, in 1967.

name: South Africa
text: African penguins live on a beach near Cape Town.

name: South Africa
text: South Africa is one of 54 UN members that drive on the left.

name: South Africa
text: South Africa's Kruger National Park, one of Africa's largest game reserves, is bigger than Switzerland.
truth: Kruger covers under 20,000 km², less than half of Switzerland's 41,300 km².

name: Lesotho
text: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.

name: Lesotho
text: All of Lesotho lies more than 1,000 metres above sea level.

name: Lesotho
text: Lesotho has a ski resort, Afriski, high in the Maloti Mountains.

name: Lesotho
text: Lesotho is one of 54 UN members that drive on the left.

name: Lesotho
text: Lesotho is the smallest country in Africa.
truth: The Seychelles is far smaller: about 460 km², against Lesotho's 30,360 km².

name: Ghana
text: Lake Volta, in Ghana, is the largest man-made lake in the world by surface area.

name: Ghana
text: The Greenwich meridian, 0 degrees longitude, runs through the Ghanaian city of Tema.

name: Ghana
text: Ghana grows more cocoa than any country except Côte d'Ivoire.

name: Ghana
text: Kente, a cloth woven in bright strips, comes from Ghana.

name: Ghana
text: The equator crosses Ghana, near the coast: it is one of only 11 UN members whose land it crosses.
truth: Ghana is not among the 11 UN members whose land the equator crosses.

name: DR Congo
text: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world: at least 220 m deep in places.

name: DR Congo
text: The okapi, a forest relative of the giraffe, lives in the wild only in DR Congo.

name: DR Congo
text: Bonobos live in the wild only in DR Congo.

name: DR Congo
text: The equator crosses DR Congo: it is one of only 11 UN members whose land it crosses.

name: DR Congo
text: The Congo is the longest river in Africa, longer even than the Nile.
truth: The Nile is longer: the Congo is Africa's second-longest river.

name: Madagascar
text: Lemurs are native to Madagascar and nowhere else.

name: Madagascar
text: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.

name: Madagascar
text: Almost half of the world's chameleon species live only on Madagascar.

name: Madagascar
text: Madagascar grows more vanilla than any other country.

name: Madagascar
text: Baobabs grow wild only on Madagascar.
truth: Baobabs also grow wild in mainland Africa and Australia; six of the eight species are found only on Madagascar.

name: Colombia
text: Colombia has more bird species than any other country: nearly 2,000.

name: Colombia
text: Colombia is the only country in South America with coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

name: Colombia
text: Colombia produces more emeralds than any other country.

name: Colombia
text: More than half of Colombia's land is forest: about 53%.

name: Colombia
text: Colombia grows more coffee than any other country, even more than Brazil.
truth: Brazil grows by far the most coffee of any country.

name: Morocco
text: At the Strait of Gibraltar, Morocco and Spain are less than 15 km apart.

name: Morocco
text: Argan oil comes from the argan tree, which grows wild almost only in south-western Morocco.

name: Morocco
text: Toubkal, in Morocco's Atlas Mountains, is the highest mountain in North Africa.

name: Morocco
text: Morocco is one of 21 UN members with a coast on the Mediterranean Sea.

name: Morocco
text: Marrakesh, at the foot of the Atlas Mountains, is the capital of Morocco.
truth: Rabat is the capital of Morocco; Casablanca is its largest city.

name: Vietnam
text: Son Doong, in Vietnam, is the largest known cave in the world.

name: Vietnam
text: Vietnam grows more coffee than any country except Brazil.

name: Vietnam
text: Ha Long Bay, in Vietnam, has about 1,600 limestone islands and islets.

name: Vietnam
text: Vietnam is one of 14 UN members that share a land border with China.

name: Vietnam
text: French explorers found Son Doong cave in the 1800s.
truth: A local man found the cave around 1990, and British cavers first explored it in 2009.

name: Greece
text: The poem behind Greece's national anthem has 158 stanzas, the longest anthem text in the world.

name: Greece
text: Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games, in 1896.

name: Greece
text: About 80% of Greece is mountainous.

name: Greece
text: Since 2002, only cheese made in Greece may be sold in the EU under the name 'feta'.

name: Greece
text: Greece has no active volcanoes: the last eruption there was more than 3,000 years ago.
truth: Santorini's volcano is active: it last erupted in 1950.

name: Singapore
text: Singapore has more than 8,000 people per square kilometre of land, the second-most of the 193 UN members.

name: Singapore
text: Singapore is more than a fifth bigger than in 1965, thanks to land reclaimed from the sea.

name: Singapore
text: Singapore's Night Safari, opened in 1994, was the first zoo in the world for animals at night.

name: Singapore
text: Jewel, at Singapore's Changi Airport, has the tallest indoor waterfall in the world, 40 m high.

name: Singapore
text: Singapore is made up of a single island, about 50 km from east to west.
truth: Singapore is made up of more than 60 islands: one main island and many small ones.

name: Bhutan
text: Gangkhar Puensum, in Bhutan, is the highest mountain in the world that nobody has climbed.

name: Bhutan
text: Bhutan's forests take in more carbon dioxide than the whole country gives off.

name: Bhutan
text: Thimphu, the capital of Bhutan, has no traffic lights.

name: Bhutan
text: Bhutan is one of 14 UN members that share a land border with China.

name: Bhutan
text: Bhutan's national animal is the snow leopard, which lives high in the mountains of the north.
truth: Bhutan's national animal is the takin.
